clue.text: Traditionalists such as Wellington or Marlborough

definitions.meaning: people of the old-fashioned type who stick to established ways
Wellington and Marlborough are long-established English private boarding schools

explanation.walkthrough: Wellington College and Marlborough College are old English private (public) schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both conservative people set in established ways and an old established school.

clue.text: Bound to take it easy before work

parts.note: to loll is to lounge lazily
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to rest before starting a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged', but it is the verb for moving in leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move in clumsy bounds, as a rabbit or puppy does.

clue.text: What monokinis have shown up? Exactly!

indicators.note: in a down clue, showing something upwards means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: a monokini is a topless swimsuit, so it has no top

explanation.surface: A question about what topless swimwear reveals, followed by an exclamation of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an idiom for precisely right, the same as an emphatic exclamation of agreement.

clue.text: House investing nothing in basic education? Hence disgust

indicators.note: in says the letter for nothing sits inside the letters for basic education

parts.note: the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A political chamber putting no money into schooling causes revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' just pictures the house putting the nought in; 'in' places it. The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is a strong feeling of disgust or revulsion, and 'hence' just links it to the wordplay.

clue.text: Pathetically, not opening sherry

indicators.note: not opening says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: doloroso is a musical direction meaning sorrowfully, plaintively

explanation.surface: A sad comment on a bottle of sherry that will not open.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLOROSO is an Italian musical direction; losing its first letter D leaves the sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, full-bodied type of Spanish sherry.

clue.text: Person mounting semi-precious stone for rich traveller

parts.note: jet is a black gemstone made from fossilised wood
a setter mounts gems in jewellery

explanation.surface: A jeweller setting a stone for a wealthy client.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet-setter is a wealthy person who flies around fashionable places.

clue.text: Carrying European writer, mount became harder to climb

indicators.note: carrying says the horse holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a steed is a horse to ride
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A horse bearing a European author found the mountain growing steeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a mountain belonging to the definition, but it is the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope that steepened grew steeper, so it became harder to climb.

clue.text: Pound provided this, oddly enough

parts.note: Pound is the poet Ezra Pound, who wrote poetry without regular metre, while a pound coin would oddly provide something that costs nothing

explanation.walkthrough: Ezra Pound was a major modernist poet; the surface suggests money.
explanation.definitionFit: Free verse is unrhymed poetry without regular metre, the form Ezra Pound championed.

clue.text: Character reference, for example

definitions.meaning: a reference is one kind of written communication

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an alphabetic symbol and a written message, such as a reference from an employer.

clue.text: With dashing young man, search for scarlet flower

parts.note: a blood is an old word for a fashionable young rake
to root is to rummage or search

explanation.surface: A dashing young man goes looking for a red flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blood' for a dashing young man is old-fashioned slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodroot is a North American plant named for its red sap, so a scarlet flower fits loosely.

clue.text: Sectarian type found in East German city, originally

parts.note: Essen is a city in western Germany

indicators.note: originally says only the first letter of the word East is wanted

explanation.surface: A member of a sect discovered in an East German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a single phrase; it splits into the initial E and the city, which comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ancient Jewish sect, so one member is a sectarian type.

clue.text: Relating to shifts of temperature in unusually cool room

indicators.note: in says the temperature letter sits inside the rearranged letters
unusually says the letters of cool room are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: Temperature changes in a strangely chilly room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns COOL ROOM into LOCOMOOR; 'in' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotor means relating to locomotion, the movement from one place to another.

clue.text: Essayist and editor said to plagiarise?

indicators.note: said says the word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: to plagiarise is to steal another's words

explanation.surface: A writer and editor is accused of copying others' work.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Richard Steele co-founded The Tatler and The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Steele was an 18th-century Irish essayist and editor of periodicals.

clue.text: What finally causes breakdown in agitated stalwarts

indicators.note: agitated says the letters of the word are shaken up

explanation.surface: Even the stoutest supporters are pushed over the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the final small burden that makes someone give way.

clue.text: Under pressure, a newspaper hit hard in piece of writing

indicators.note: in a down clue, under says the remaining letters come below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a rag is a derogatory word for a newspaper
to rap is to strike
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A newspaper under pressure is hit hard over an article.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a section of a piece of writing.

clue.text: Point to a part of Spain — not hard to find Spanish city

parts.note: S is the compass point south

indicators.note: not hard says the letter H, for hard, is taken out

parts.note: La Mancha is a region of central Spain

explanation.surface: Directions to a region of Spain, ending in an easy-to-find city.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamanca is a historic university city in western Spain.

clue.text: Sound made by opening bottle of hock

definitions.meaning: the noise a cork makes as it comes out
to hock something is to pawn it

explanation.walkthrough: To pop is British slang for to pawn; hock in the surface is a German white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the short explosive noise of a cork and slang for pawning goods.

clue.text: Pages including article that's trivial reading matter

indicators.note: including says the abbreviation for pages holds the article inside

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A few pages containing an item of light reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Pap is worthless or trivial entertainment or reading.

clue.text: Energy put into one's financial provision, initially

definitions.meaning: an old British savings scheme known by the initials of Personal Equity Plan

explanation.walkthrough: A PEP was a UK tax-free investment plan, later replaced by the ISA.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means vigour and is the initialism of a personal savings plan.

clue.text: A bishop entertained by a priest in state

indicators.note: entertained by says the first pair goes inside the second

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is hosted by a priest in some state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is a state in the southern United States.

clue.text: Not having any view, vote in favour, say? Not so

indicators.note: say signals the spoken sound of the word

parts.note: aye is a yes vote
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Someone without opinions is asked to vote yes, but declines.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeless means blind, unable to see anything at all.

clue.text: Just beat seed

definitions.meaning: a small fruit seed, as in an apple

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to win by a whisker and also a small fruit seed.

clue.text: One identifies a boozer where sinning is rampant

indicators.note: rampant suggests the letters running wild

explanation.surface: A pub sign marks the place where wickedness runs riot.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn sign is the board hung outside a pub to show its name.

clue.text: A name conferred on leader of totally imperial rule

definitions.text: A name conferred on leader of totally imperial rule

indicators.note: conferred on says the following pieces are added after the earlier ones
leader of says the first letter of totally is taken

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India

explanation.surface: A title given to the head of a total empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the Roman emperor, whose name rules totally.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor, a leader of imperial rule.

clue.text: Pirate opposed by one man on board with cross

parts.note: v for versus, meaning against
I is the Roman numeral one
the chess king is the piece topped by a cross

explanation.surface: A pirate is challenged by a single sailor bearing a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikings were Norse seafaring raiders, effectively pirates.

clue.text: Authoritarian ploy mostly accepted by revered person

indicators.note: accepted by says the trimmed word goes inside the saint's abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is lost

parts.note: a trick is a ruse

explanation.surface: A dictatorial scheme mostly endorsed by a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict person demands obedience, just like an authoritarian.

clue.text: Poet's unworthy contribution to blind ignorance

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poet's inadequate input to blind ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: Indign is an archaic poetic word meaning unworthy or undeserving.

clue.text: Is taken in by popular rock musician making demands

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: taken in by says the given word goes inside the musician's name

parts.note: Sting is the English rock singer of the Police

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by a famous rock star who keeps asking for things.
explanation.definitionFit: Insisting means demanding something firmly.

clue.text: Sailor beat to eastward in ship in Med

indicators.note: in an across clue, east is to the right, so the beating word follows

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to tan is to thrash

explanation.surface: A sailor beats east in a Mediterranean ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartan is a single-masted sailing vessel of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Shares added to original one, showing growths in tropical sector

indicators.note: added to says the shares come after the single one

parts.note: the first, single share, a divi being a share of profits
divis are shares or dividends

explanation.surface: Extra shares are given to a first investor in a tropical region.
explanation.walkthrough: Divi is British slang for a dividend.
explanation.definitionFit: Divi-divi is a tropical American tree, so these are trees growing in the tropics.

clue.text: South American animals caught in areas on mountain

indicators.note: on says the rest is attached after the mountain

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: in says the caught letter sits between the area letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, twice
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Animals from South America are trapped on mountain slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpacas are domesticated camelids of the Andes; the plural can be the same as the singular.

clue.text: Special thing, being welcomed by monarch bestowing honour

indicators.note: being welcomed by says the rearranged letters go inside the monarch

parts.note: a king is a monarch

indicators.note: special suggests the word thing is made into something unusual

explanation.surface: Something special is received by the monarch giving out honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' is the anagram signal, rearranging the letters of 'thing' before they go into the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Knighting means conferring a knighthood, an honour.
